name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Subramanyam holds a roughly 10-to-1 fundraising edge with $583,000 on hand
District leans Democratic by six points in a favorable environment
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 94-95 percent
No outside spending against the incumbent and no public polling
model.rationale: Subramanyam's overwhelming financial advantage, the district's Democratic lean, and markets pricing his win odds around 95 percent leave Beckwith without a visible path, pointing to a double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Subramanyam or any polling showing the race inside single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 10th District, covering Northern Virginia suburbs including Loudoun and Prince William counties, leans Democratic by about six points. First-term incumbent Suhas Subramanyam is seeking re-election against Republican Dave Beckwith, a challenger with minimal financial backing. An independent candidate, Ahsen Malik, is also on the ballot.

Subramanyam has raised roughly $1.17 million and holds about $583,000 on hand, dwarfing Beckwith's $107,000 raised, and no outside groups have spent against him. Prediction markets place his chances around 94 to 95 percent. With no public polling available, the outlook rests on the district's lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and market pricing, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
